posts.content:
Ledger Atom được công bố trong bối cảnh nhà sản xuất ví cứng đang chịu nhiều áp lực sau vụ tấn công đánh cắp hơn 100 triệu USD tài sản của khách hàng mới đây.

Ledger hé lộ ví cứng mới dạng smartphone Android. Ảnh: Ledger

Tối ngày 15/10, công ty chế tạo ví cứng crypto Ledger đã công bố những hình ảnh đầu tiên về Atom - thế hệ ví cứng mới sử dụng thiết kế đột phá không khác gì một chiếc smartphone.

Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that. Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum ready device. Agents propose. You approve. Your Ledger signer enforces.

Máy có màn hình AMOLED 60 Hz kích thước 6.8 inch, có sẵn kính cường lực Gorilla Glass 3, có camera 50 MP quay phim 4K ở 60fps, pin 4000mAh, cảm ứng vân tay và nặng khoảng 250g.

Mặc dù vậy, Atom sẽ không có chức năng nghe gọi và lắp thẻ SIM truyền thống, thay vào đó chỉ cho phép kết nối 4G/5G đến Internet thông qua eSIM. Máy sử dụng hệ điều hành Android, đồng nghĩa với việc hỗ trợ tất cả các ứng dụng của hệ sinh thái này, cũng như tích hợp sẵn AI OpenClaw. Người dùng sẽ có tùy chọn chuyển đổi chức năng của thiết bị từ smartphone sang ví cứng để đề cao công tác bảo mật tài sản mã hóa.

Cấu hình của Ledger Atom. Ảnh: Ledger

Đặc biệt, Ledger còn thiết lập sẵn nhiều tính năng bảo mật để cho thấy đây là thiết bị lưu trữ khóa crypto tiên tiến nhất thị trường hiện tại. Atom sẽ có nút gạt vật lý để chuyển sang chế độ riêng tư, khi ấy thì máy sẽ tự động ngắt kết nối camera và microphone để đảm bảo bảo mật khi người dùng thao tác. Ngoài ra, mỗi khi người dùng tương tác với tài sản số hay private key , hệ điều hành của máy sẽ tự động chuyển sang Ledger OS, yêu cầu người dùng xác minh thông tin dưới dạng mã PIN trước khi có thể tiếp tục, đồng thời cam kết thông tin hiển thị trên màn hình là không thể hiển thị sai hay bị phishing.

Ledger còn định đưa hệ thống Agent Intent vào Atom, cho phép người dùng ký duyệt các giao dịch được đề xuất bởi AI agents mà không tiết lộ private key.

Các tính năng bảo mật của Ledger Atom. Ảnh: Ledger

Giá bán dự kiến của Atom sẽ là 849 USD cho phiên bản đăng ký đặt mua trước, sau nâng lên 899 USD sau khi ví ra mắt chính thức vào giữa năm 2027. Đây là mức giá tương đương một chiếc smartphone cao cấp và cũng lập kỷ lục giá bán của Ledger, đắt hơn gấp đôi ví cao cấp nhất hiện tại là Ledger Flex.

Ngoài ra, Ledger sẽ hợp tác cùng Solana Mobile để hỗ trợ ứng dụng Seeker, biến đây trở thành lần bắt tay đầu tiên của một nhà chế tạo ví cứng với một công ty sản xuất smartphone dành riêng cho crypto. Đáng chú ý, báo CoinDesk tiết lộ hoạt động chế tạo và lắp ráp của Atom sẽ diễn ra tại nhà máy của công ty đặt tại Việt Nam.

Sự kiện ra mắt Ledger Atom diễn ra trong bối cảnh Ledger vẫn đang xử lý hậu quả của sự cố bảo mật mới đây ảnh hưởng đến hàng trăm người dùng, với thiệt hại ước tính lên đến 102 triệu USD .

Trong cập nhật mới nhất, công ty thừa nhận đã xảy ra một vụ tấn công nhắm vào chuỗi cung ứng của mình, theo đó một tổ chức tội phạm chưa rõ danh tính đã mua thiết bị Ledger suốt nhiều tháng qua, sau đó cài các linh kiện trái phép vào và đưa chúng về lại các nhà phân phối chính thức của hãng tại khu vực Đông Nam Á. Đến đầu tháng 10, kẻ xấu đã quyết định kích hoạt lỗ hổng này và bòn rút tiền của người dùng ví cứng.

How a company behaves when it is attacked says more about it than any product launch. Here is where we stand on the hardware implant attack: what happened, how we responded, and what we are changing. Read the blog here, and watch the keynote live at 2pm CET: https://t.co/uFpK8BhMQs

Ledger tiếp tục khẳng định công nghệ lõi của mình, bao gồm chip, hệ điều hành và server, không bị ảnh hưởng, do đó sự cố chỉ giới hạn ở các thiết bị đã bị can thiệp vào chứ không lan rộng toàn cầu như một số thông tin trước đó.

Để xử lý hậu quả trước mắt, công ty đã yêu cầu các nhà phân phối của mình ở Đông Nam Á và Hong Kong dừng bán ví cứng, đồng thời kiểm kê kho hàng trên toàn cầu để phát hiện các lô ví có thể đã bị can thiệp khác.

Tuy nhiên, Ledger lại không đề cập gì đến khả năng bồi thường cho người dùng, hay phản hồi các báo cáo về việc một số thiết bị phân phối ở Châu Âu cũng bị dính linh kiện lạ .

Ledger hé lộ ví cứng mới dạng smartphone Android. Ảnh: Ledger

Tối ngày 15/10, công ty chế tạo ví cứng crypto Ledger đã công bố những hình ảnh đầu tiên về Atom - thế hệ ví cứng mới sử dụng thiết kế đột phá không khác gì một chiếc smartphone.

Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that. Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum ready device. Agents propose. You approve. Your Ledger signer enforces.

Máy có màn hình AMOLED 60 Hz kích thước 6.8 inch, có sẵn kính cường lực Gorilla Glass 3, có camera 50 MP quay phim 4K ở 60fps, pin 4000mAh, cảm ứng vân tay và nặng khoảng 250g.

Mặc dù vậy, Atom sẽ không có chức năng nghe gọi và lắp thẻ SIM truyền thống, thay vào đó chỉ cho phép kết nối 4G/5G đến Internet thông qua eSIM. Máy sử dụng hệ điều hành Android, đồng nghĩa với việc hỗ trợ tất cả các ứng dụng của hệ sinh thái này, cũng như tích hợp sẵn AI OpenClaw. AI agents keep coming back for crypto as x402 wallet refill rate surges to 89%

Chainalysis reports rising repeat funding among active wallets, while median time to first payment has collapsed from 73 days to just 18 minutes.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Chainalysis found that nearly nine in 10 qualifying x402 wallets received fresh funding within 30 days as AI crypto payments accelerated. 02 Median time to first payment plunged from 73 days to 18 minutes, signaling growing use of stablecoins for automated transactions. 03 With x402 transactions surpassing 138 million, payment providers face a test of whether recurring wallet activity can sustain profitable businesses. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Two-thirds of newly funded x402 wallets made payments within an hour in the third quarter, signaling growing adoption of automated cryptocurrency transactions.

The proportion jumped from just 4% a year earlier, according to a new Chainalysis report . The median time between a wallet's initial funding and its first payment also collapsed to 18 minutes from 73 days in late 2025, suggesting software developers are increasingly allocating funds for immediate transactions.

The findings mark a shift in the emerging market for machine-to-machine payments, where AI agents can purchase data, computing resources, and digital services using stablecoins. By July, Coinbase's x402 standard on the Base blockchain had processed more than 138 million transactions as technology companies explored ways to monetize automated services.

AI agents move beyond experimental payments

Coinbase developed x402 in 2025, letting software applications pay for online resources directly through web requests and eliminating the need for users to manually authorize each purchase.

The technology lets AI agents request information or computing services, receive a payment instruction, and settle the transaction in cryptocurrency before accessing the requested resource.

Its appeal lies partly in the economics of micropayments, where conventional banking and card-processing charges can exceed the value of the underlying purchase.

Chainalysis found that more than 87% of x402 payments during the 16 months through September ranged between $0.0001 and $0.10, with transactions worth between one and 10 cents accounting for the most common payment size.

These small transactions increasingly support per-request services, including AI model inference, code reviews, financial intelligence, and data retrieval.

The model lets developers buy computing resources as needed, potentially opening new revenue streams for businesses that previously relied on subscriptions or enterprise contracts.

The shift is also becoming visible in how frequently wallets receive additional funding.

Of the x402 wallets that transacted on at least two separate days, Chainalysis found that 89.3% of those first funded in the second quarter of 2026 received another deposit within 30 days.

That compares with 70.6% for wallets first funded in the third quarter of 2025, pointing to more consistent financing among active participants.

The analytics firm attributed the increase to developers moving beyond one-time experiments and establishing recurring spending budgets for automated software.

Early x402 activity had been heavily influenced by speculative token launches and short-lived applications.

However, Chainalysis found millions of subsequent payments flowing toward information services and AI infrastructure, suggesting that demand is increasingly extending into software-related purchases.

AI model inference, which lets applications pay for responses generated by other AI systems, has become one of the protocol's largest transaction categories.

US developers dominate emerging AI payment economy

American companies have emerged as the leading participants in this new market, reflecting their concentration of AI developers, stablecoin issuers, and cryptocurrency infrastructure providers.

Chainalysis estimates that US-attributed wallets account for approximately 30% of geographically identified transactions between AI agents and service providers.

Their dominance is particularly pronounced in AI model inference, where American-linked wallets generated 88.1% of payments.

US wallets also accounted for 41.8% of payments to agent frameworks and development tools, alongside 23.2% of transactions involving data and search services.

This concentration positions American infrastructure providers, including Coinbase and Circle , to benefit if machine-to-machine commerce becomes a meaningful market for dollar-denominated stablecoins.

BlackRock's head of digital assets research, Will Su, told Chainalysis that the investment firm is closely monitoring the sector, with autonomous agents potentially generating continuous demand for small payments throughout the day.

China is showing a different activity pattern.

Chinese-linked wallets accounted for about 90% of geographically attributed payments for security and code-analysis services, much of which went to AgentLISA, a platform that uses AI to audit blockchain smart contracts.

However, Chinese wallets represented just 0.1% of identified AI model inference transactions.

Chainalysis suggested the difference may reflect Chinese developers' greater reliance on open-weight AI models, including DeepSeek and Qwen, which can run without paying an external provider for every request.

That division could influence which companies capture revenue as automated software becomes a more active participant in digital commerce.

Growing transaction volumes face a commercial test

The rapid expansion of x402 has also raised questions about how much recorded activity represents spending between independent businesses.

A July academic study examining 136.7 million x402 settlements worth $44.1 million on Base found that 21.2% of transactions were fictitious, including self-payments and closed transaction loops.

Another 63.78% occurred within clusters of wallets linked through funding relationships, which can include transactions between related operators as well as legitimate commercial activity.

The researchers identified approximately $187,861 in payments reaching recognizable services without detected connections between buyers and sellers. Their broader estimate placed potentially genuine economic activity as high as $20.26 million.

Those findings highlight a commercial challenge for companies building around automated payments: translating rising transaction activity into revenue from customers purchasing services independently.

Related Reading AI agents employ $24M market to act smarter as agentic crypto payments spread online

The economics are particularly demanding when individual transactions are worth fractions of a cent. Merchants must generate sufficient recurring purchases to cover computing, infrastructure, and operating costs, while payment providers need enough settlement activity to support their own businesses.

The July study found that 25,163 listed Base resources corresponded to 811 distinct payment recipients, with just 249 earning at least $10 during the observation period.

As more AI developers introduce pay-per-request services, growth in recurring merchant receipts will more clearly indicate which businesses can sustain themselves beyond the initial surge in automated payments.

Decrypt News Markets Ethereum, Altcoins See 'Outsized Drawdowns' Due to Macro Pressures

Market analysts say that macro factors are pushing altcoin prices down, after ETH, XRP, and SOL all dropped on the day.

By Ryan S. Gladwin Edited by Stephen Graves

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Ethereum, XRP, and Solana have all dropped in value on the day, with "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin.

Experts point to Wednesday's consumer price index coming in at 3.7% and expectations of an October interest rate hike as major macro pressures.

The slide is also a natural hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.

Altcoins have taken a hit over the past 24 hours, with major tokens seeing "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin. Experts say that this has largely been prompted by macro pressures pushing prices down.

With the market cap of all cryptocurrencies dropping by 2.5% to $2.8 trillion, Ethereum dropped by 5.5% to a $289 billion market cap over the past 24 hours, XRP fell by 5.1% to $82.4 billion, and Solana slipped by 3.8% to $60.6 billion. Meanwhile, industry leader Bitcoin has slipped by 3.1% on the day and 2.6% on the week, sitting at a market cap of $1.6 trillion.

It comes after the consumer price index rose 3.7% in the year to September, as Decrypt reported on Wednesday, with Myriad predictors pointing to a 28% chance of an October interest rate hike (Disclaimer: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt 's parent company Dastan).

Nick Forster, founder of options trading exchange Derive.xyz, said in a note shared with Decrypt that this shifted traders into "protection mode" as "hedging activity" on the platform doubled, and whales pulled back on optimistic bets made in spring.

"This immediate pull-back from long-term upside bets alongside aggressive short-term hedging shows a dramatic regime shift," he said, "with institutional participants rapidly reassessing their macro risk exposure as the path for interest rates turns murky again."

When markets react like this, Luke Nolan, senior research associate at CoinShares, says that altcoins are impacted the most.

"[It] seems to be high beta assets just got hit harder, similar to in equities as well, where the high flyers have seen outsized drawdowns in recent sessions," Nolan told Decrypt . "Alts are typically more sensitive to financial conditions, and tightening affects the premise of liquidity expanding."

Nolan also highlighted the U.S. dollar hitting a near 18-month high as a downward pressure on the entire crypto market. He said that over a medium-term horizon, crypto tends to have an inverse correlation to the US Dollar Index, or DXY. This is partly due to crypto being priced in dollars, Nolan explained, but also because a rising dollar causes a tightening in liquidity and a fall in risk appetite.

Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt that the slide is also a hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.

Since the start of October, futures open interest in altcoins (excluding Ethereum) has fallen by $8 billion, Shannon said. To him, that shows traders have “taken chips off the table,” which is a natural reaction after such a strong run.

That pattern is playing out with Ethereum, he added. ETH outperformed Bitcoin for three consecutive months, the first time it’s managed that since March 2021, and investors have been cashing in since. Ethereum ETFs saw 11 straight trading days of net outflows totalling $782.8 million, he said, before a brief inflow on Tuesday. Money has been heading back out since, per CoinGlass data, with $129.5 million in net outflows.

"This price action is more of a consolidation period for altcoins that have already done well," Shannon told Decrypt . "Altcoins generally tend to exhibit high correlations with BTC in tough times and lower correlations, especially with idiosyncratic catalysts, in better market environments. Hence, for the near term, it is possible that these altcoins trade in lockstep with BTC, albeit more sensitively."

For prices to recover, Nolan says he wants to see expectations of an interest rate hike in October to fall. Right now, he struggles to call a bottom for altcoins as he sees valid arguments for movements in either direction.

"I could see a situation where Bitcoin loses its support and altcoins likely bleed further," Nolan told Decrypt . "The opposite could also be true: this could be just a short-term correction, and we could be back into decent market conditions soon, which if Bitcoin was to push back decently above 80k, I could very well see an outsized up move for altcoins."

Written by Helen Partz staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Helen Partz staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor

Russia to ban direct peer-to-peer crypto trades starting July 2027

Latest News Published Oct 15, 2026 Russia plans to ban direct P2P crypto trades from July 1, 2027, while separate rules already prohibit transfers from digital accounts to self-custody wallets.

Russia will ban direct peer-to-peer (P2P) cryptocurrency transactions between individuals starting next year, requiring individuals to use authorized intermediaries for such trades.

The restriction will end individuals’ ability to exchange crypto assets directly without intermediaries, the Bank of Russia, the country’s central bank, explained in guidance updated Monday. The regulator confirmed that such transactions will remain permitted only until July 1, 2027.

The regulator also clarified that individuals are not allowed to transfer crypto assets from their digital accounts to their own non-custodial, or self-custodial, wallets.

The move comes as Russia expands its regulated crypto market. On Monday, the Bank of Russia authorized Sberbank , the country’s largest bank, to offer crypto exchange services after earlier approving it as a digital asset custodian.

The approval follows Russia’s new crypto rules, which came into force on Sept. 1 and brought exchange operators and custodians under central bank oversight. The country also continues to prohibit cryptocurrency payments for goods and services.

Industry executives have previously told Cointelegraph that restrictions on P2P crypto trading and noncustodial wallets may be difficult to enforce. Jan3 CEO Samson Mow said P2P trading is more resilient to regulatory crackdowns than centralized platforms, while SatoshiLabs executive Stepan Uherik said wallet app bans would leave hardware and desktop wallets unaffected .

Russia to ban direct peer-to-peer crypto trades starting July 2027

Latest News Published Oct 15, 2026 Russia plans to ban direct P2P crypto trades from July 1, 2027, while separate rules already prohibit transfers from digital accounts to self-custody wallets.

Russia will ban direct peer-to-peer (P2P) cryptocurrency transactions between individuals starting next year, requiring individuals to use authorized intermediaries for such trades.

The restriction will end individuals’ ability to exchange crypto assets directly without intermediaries, the Bank of Russia, the country’s central bank, explained in guidance updated Monday. The regulator confirmed that such transactions will remain permitted only until July 1, 2027.

The regulator also clarified that individuals are not allowed to transfer crypto assets from their digital accounts to their own non-custodial, or self-custodial, wallets.

The move comes as Russia expands its regulated crypto market. On Monday, the Bank of Russia authorized Sberbank , the country’s largest bank, to offer crypto exchange services after earlier approving it as a digital asset custodian.

The approval follows Russia’s new crypto rules, which came into force on Sept. 1 and brought exchange operators and custodians under central bank oversight. The country also continues to prohibit cryptocurrency payments for goods and services.

Industry executives have previously told Cointelegraph that restrictions on P2P crypto trading and noncustodial wallets may be difficult to enforce. Jan3 CEO Samson Mow said P2P trading is more resilient to regulatory crackdowns than centralized platforms, while SatoshiLabs executive Stepan Uherik said wallet app bans would leave hardware and desktop wallets unaffected .

Nasdaq-listed Tron sets up $200M ATM share offering to fuel TRX acquisitions

Latest News Published Oct 15, 2026 The Nasdaq-listed treasury company holds about $237 million in TRX tokens and plans to raise additional capital to fund its purchases, alongside its daily accumulation.

Nasdaq-listed Tron (TRON) has filed for a new at-the-market (ATM) share offering allowing it to sell up to $200 million of common stock that will fund an even-larger Tron (TRX) treasury.

The deal allows Tron to periodically sell shares of its common stock at $0.0001 par value through Clear Street, which acts as an agent and retains a commission of up to 3% of gross proceeds, according to a Wednesday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The company’s existing TRX accumulation program , announced in February, called for the purchase of approximately $50,000 worth of TRX per day for 360 consecutive days. Tron’s treasury holds 718.9 million TRX tokens, currently worth about $237 million, after the company’s latest acquisition of 149,369 TRX at an average price of $0.3347 on Thursday.

posts.content:
GMGN is a cryptocurrency trading platform with a twist. It’s designed to help users discover, analyze, and trade meme coins.

It provides real-time token data, smart money tracking, wallet analytics, automated trading tools, and more in a single interface, along with a range of other features that I will be exploring in this review.

Overall, the goal is to make it easier to spot emerging opportunities in the fast-moving trenches market.

Unlike traditional cryptocurrency exchanges, GMGN is focused entirely on on-chain trading activity. Users are able to monitor profitable wallets, track newly launched tokens and analyze different patterns. They can also execute trades without having to switch between multiple platforms.

In the following review, I will take a look at some of its key features, supported networks, trading fees, security, and overall usability. The goal is to help you decide whether it’s the right platform for your specific trading needs and requirements.

GMGN is hosting a major global trading championship that starts on October 16th. It will feature 10 days of relentless live, on-chain trading, with the top six users heading to a Grand Final in London during the flagship conference Solana Breakpoint. Entry is completely free and the champion will win a custom Aston Martin Vantage. Check out the GMGN Global Championship and sign up here .

As mentioned above, GMGN is a multi-chain cryptocurrency trading platform. It’s designed to help you discover, analyze, and ultimately trade meme coins. The protocol combines real-time market data with wallet tracking, token security checks, and automated trading tools. You can access this through a single interface, which is convenient.

GMGN aggregates on-chain information to help you identify trading opportunities and analyze the activity of a certain token. You can explore trending tokens, search using contract addresses, examine price charts, as well as monitor transactions from other wallets.

The platform also supports automated trading through limit orders, take-profit, and stop-loss settings. It also features copy trading. You can configure various execution parameters, including slippage tolerance and priority fees. This can help you manage the way your transactions are prioritized and processed.

GMGN supports multiple networks. These include:

However, the protocol also supports cross-chain integration support for networks such as Solana, BSC, Rohinhood, Base, ETH, Arbitrum, Stable, Arc, Xlayer, HyperEVM, MegaETH, Monad, and Tron.

Now, GMGN is primarily suited to active meme coin traders who look for real-time market insights and advanced trading capabilities. Its wallet tracking and copy trading tools, however, may also appeal to users who want to monitor experienced traders. That said, if you have no previous experience in dabbling in the world of on-chain meme coin trading, there might be a learning curve to go through.

That said, beginners can use GMGN to explore tokens and analyze market activity. Of course, most of its advanced capabilities make understanding of on-chain transactions and adjacent trading risks very important.

GMGN provides a range of different tools that can help you discover new meme coins, analyze on-chain activity, and execute trades. Let’s have a look at some of the most important ones.

The platform’s core functionality allows you to discover newly launched and trending tokens through dedicated market lists. You can filter tokens using various criteria, including but not limited to market capitalization, transaction activity, price movements, and trading volume.

Every single token has a dedicated page that displays price charts, transaction histories, holder information, and trading activity. GMGN is also designed to support cross-chain multicharts, allowing users to monitor multiple charts at the same time.

These features can help you identify emerging tokens and compare market activity. You won’t have to switch between multiple analytics platforms, which is a considerable benefit.

The platform’s smart money tracking feature is designed to allow you to monitor wallet addresses that are associated with profitable traders, whales, and other market participants that you may find interesting.

You can follow individual wallets and receive notifications when those addresses execute transactions. Trading activity can also be categorized by the type of wallet, including KOLs, smart money, developers, and snipers.

Another notable feature is Wallet Radar, which helps users identify profitable wallets by analyzing trading activity across the selected tokens. Some of the factors used to categorize addresses include:

You can analyze multiple tokens at the same time and add discovered addresses to your list for copy trading. Naturally, this brings me to the next feature.

Now, copy trading has become particularly popular in the crypto space, and GMGN supports automated copy trading, which allows you to replicate buying and selling made by selected wallet addresses.

You can configure fixed purchase amounts or set maximum follow-buy limits. Selling options also include automatically copying a wallet’s sales or using separate take-profit and stop-loss conditions.

The platform also offers a Lightning Mode. This is designed to accelerate trade execution while copy trading. However, it’s worth noting that this introduces additional risks because it uses unconfirmed blockchain transaction data.

All in all, copy trading can definitely save time, but users should also account for slippage, transaction costs, as well as the differences between the original trade and its execution.

This is another very important feature for on-chain traders because a lot of the upcoming and trending meme coins have not been verified by anyone. That’s why GMGN includes token security checks that can help you identify potentially suspicious assets.

Depending on the network, the platform can display indicators such as:

These checks can help you assess common warning signs before committing to a trade. Of course, these can never guarantee complete accuracy and even GMGN recommends consulting multiple security tools before coming to a conclusion.

GMGN offers several features that are designed to automate trade execution and manage your positions.

Traders are able to place instant buy and sell orders, configure limit orders, and establish automatic take-profit or stop-loss strategies.

Specialized automated trading strategies such as Dev Sell are also included. This allows you to trigger a sale when a token creator sells a specified portion of their holdings. There are also Migrated Sells, which allow the user to automate selling when eligible Solana tokens migrate to a decentralized exchange liquidity pool. This is important for those traders who participate in launchpads such as Pump.fun, for instance.

On top of that, users are able to adjust execution settings such as slippage tolerance, priority fees, and Anti-MEV protection. The latter is designed to reduce exposure to sandwich attacks. However, stronger transaction protection could also involve additional fees or slower execution, so it’s a trade-off that you would have to consider.

It’s also important to understand that while all of these features reduce the need for constant market monitoring, automated transactions remain subject to other factors such as liquidity conditions, execution failures, network congestion, and more – all of which bring challenges that you need to take into account.

Another interesting feature is the ability to analyze a lot of compiled data. GMGN provides wallet-level analytics. These allow you to examine transaction histories and evaluate trading performance. You can then use the conclusions to determine whether a certain trader is worth following.

You can review metrics such as realized and unrealized profit, total buying and selling activity, average purchase prices, and current holdings.

The platform also displays historical trading activity, making it possible to investigate how individual wallets have interacted with particular tokens.

These analytics complement GMGN’s tracking and copy trading features by helping users assess wallet activity before deciding whether to follow another trader.

However, wallet performance data should be considered alongside transaction costs and market conditions, as historical profitability does not guarantee future returns.

Getting started with the platform is going to feel incredibly familiar to anyone who has previously done any sort of on-chain trading and a bit intimidating for those who are new to it. That said, the learning curve is not that steep once you get the hang of it.

GMGN does a fairly good job of dividing the interface in clear sections, which become easy to follow once you connect your wallet.

Once you have landed on the homepage, you can select your preferred blockchain network and start exploring trending meme coins, newly launched tokens, and market activity. If you don’t want to trade, that’s fine, you’re not required to. GMGN also allows you to search for specific tokens using their contract addresses.

When you’re ready to trade, you can connect a compatible wallet or log in through Telegram, which can expand the available automated trading features.

GMGN supports different types of wallet connection methods including Telegram-based wallets and compatible Web3 wallets such as Phantom and MetaMask, for example.

Once you have done that, you can select the deposit option, which is found in your account tab in the top-right section of the main navigation menu.

Once the wallet is funded, you can browse GMGN’s token discovery lists or search for a token using its contract address.

Before trading, you can review price charts, liquidity, transaction activity, holder distribution, and available security indicators.

To execute a trade, users select the desired token, enter the purchase amount, and configure transaction settings such as slippage tolerance and priority fees. They can then submit the transaction through the trading interface.

GMGN also allows you to configure automated orders and exit strategies, including take-profit and stop-loss conditions.

Before confirming a transaction, you should review the expected execution costs. GMGN charges a 1% trading fee, while blockchain gas fees, priority fees, tips, and any applicable token launchpad fees may increase the total cost.

GMGN is a well-known and established name in the world of on-chain crypto trading. It provides several safety features, but it’s important to know that these do not eliminate the possibility of losses or malicious activity pertaining to events that are not directly associated with the platform itself. That said, let’s have a look.

GMGN supports external Web3 wallets alongside Telegram-based wallets for automated trading.

Now, when you connect an external wallet, you retain full responsibility for protecting your private keys and recovery phrases.

In essence, if you connect your wallet, you retain full custody of your funds. However, if you decide to use the Telegram bot, then you also need to export the private key of the newly created wallet. That said, there are caveats, so I highly recommend that you check here .

Despite the non-custodial model, there are several risks that you need to account for, all of which are not really manageable by the platform but stem from the nature of trading meme coins and newly launched cryptocurrencies.

GMGN also discussed these at length in their documentation. Overall, though, the platform provides a useful set of security and risk-analysis tools but as with all on-chain platforms, it shouldn’t be considered risk-free.

If you are an on-chain trader, GMGN is absolutely worth using. It offers valuable tools for discovering up-and-coming tokens, meme coins, analyzing on-chain activity, and automating trading strategies. Its combination of

posts.titleVi: Toobit Reveals Revamped Futures Trading Experience
posts.summary: The popular and award-winning international cryptocurrency exchange Toobit announced a series of upgrades to Toobit Futures.
posts.summaryVi: The popular and award-winning international cryptocurrency exchange Toobit announced a series of upgrades to Toobit Futures.
posts.content:
The popular and award-winning international cryptocurrency exchange Toobit announced a series of upgrades to Toobit Futures.

The platform introduced a series of changes, including a redesigned trading interface, faster order execution, and enhanced position management and tracking tools.

The revamped Toobit Futures web interface comes with a much more intuitive trading panel, clearer order parameters, and customizable layouts and display settings.

In addition, users can also take advantage of keyboard shortcuts, one-click trading, faster trading pair search and switching, which further simplify order placement and navigation.

A new data timeline is also designed to display trading activity and position changes in a chronological way, making it a lot easier to review past transactions. An important improvement is separate isolated margin mode. It allows users to maintain many independent positions in the same direction on a single trading pair.

Unlike the previous approach of calculating positions collectively, now each position has its own profit and loss, margin allocation, and liquidation price calculations. This is intended to allow traders to manage different entry points, exit targets, and risk exposure separately. The feature is going to be first available in Demo Trading on the web and app version 2.3.8, with live support planned for a subsequent release.

The move is designed to make the overall futures trading experience a lot faster, more intuitive, and easier to manage. The interface brings key trading functions together in a way that is more accessible and clearer, while also featuring customizable display settings that allow users to tailor the platform to their specific preferences.

Moreover, the faster order execution, one-click trading, and keyboard shortcuts also help streamline the trading process, particularly for active traders who are looking for means to respond quickly to market movements.

The upgrade comes amid substantial activity in the field of cryptocurrency derivatives trading. According to CoinGlass’s 2026 Semi-Annual Cryptocurrency Derivatives Market Report, derivatives trading volume reached $35.08 trillion in the first half of 2026, averaging $193.8 billion daily. Average daily open interest stood at $112.7 billion, underscoring the importance of effective position monitoring and risk management.

posts.summary: Bitcoin is witnessing a decline in buying pressure, according to crypto analytics platform Alphractal. The latest reading of the Buy/Sell Pressure Delta indicates that bullish momentum is starting to cool. Alphractal outlined two possible outcomes when the metric stops climbing.

posts.content:
Bitcoin is witnessing a decline in buying pressure, according to crypto analytics platform Alphractal. The latest reading of the Buy/Sell Pressure Delta indicates that bullish momentum is starting to cool.

Alphractal outlined two possible outcomes when the metric stops climbing.

Bitcoin could face a decline, or it could move sideways and enter a consolidation phase. In past market cycles, both patterns have appeared before larger price moves, including deeper corrections.

For now, the dip in buying pressure is not a major warning sign on its own. The bigger concern would be a continued decline over several days. If the metric turns negative, it could signal that sellers are gaining control.

Interestingly, Bitcoin plunged briefly towards $80,000. The world’s largest crypto asset has since recovered modestly as it trades at $81,200. While it’s still early to say if bulls are losing their buying momentum, Joao Wedson believes that the impact will always be “greater” on altcoins.

But Wedson also flagged a historical pattern that could add to the uncertainty in the altcoin market. According to the Alphractal founder, when the median performance of the top 100 altcoins outpaces Bitcoin, a period of increased volatility often follows. This outperformance rarely lasts for long, and market trends typically reverse around every 60 days. During these changes, capital tends to flow back into BTC and stablecoins. If the pattern holds, altcoins could face increased selling pressure as traders adjust their positions.

This could make the coming weeks more volatile, especially if Bitcoin’s buying momentum continues to weaken.

BTC’s start to October has been far from the strong run traders have come to expect from “Uptober.” With the month yet to deliver much upside, Bernardo Brites, Co-Founder and CEO of Trace Finance, offered a different take on why the usual October rally may not play out as expected. While speaking to CryptoPotato , Brites said,

“A roughly flat October so far challenges the narrative more than the market. Uptober was always a pattern, not a law. Ten green Octobers in thirteen years is a strong record, but it’s a small sample, mostly from a market driven by retail momentum and leverage. And last year already broke a six-year streak. Today Bitcoin trades more on ETF flows, rates, and the dollar, and none of those follow the calendar. This month’s real catalyst is the Fed meeting on October 27 and 28. If October ends green, that’s where it will come from.”

Decrypt News Business Ledger Announces Atom Touchscreen Android Device

Ledger says the Android-based Atom will carry anti-tamper protections and be sold only on its site, as it probes tampered resold wallets.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Ledger has announced Atom, a touchscreen Android device that incorporates a Secure Element running Ledger OS.

Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner, with its Seeker app and Solana dApp Store preinstalled on Ledger's new Atom device.

The launch comes as Ledger investigates hidden implants found in hardware wallets sold through a reseller in Southeast Asia.

Ledger's new Atom device will ship with Solana's Seeker app preinstalled, the companies announced on stage at Ledger's Op3n conference in Paris on Thursday.

Billed as a "signer" rather than a hardware wallet, the Atom is an Android-powered touchscreen device equipped with a data-only eSIM and Ledger's Secure Element, enabling users to send and receive encrypted messages with other Atom users as well as perform crypto transactions in the manner of its range of wallets. To do so, the device switches into a Ledger OS-powered "Secure Mode" for sensitive operations such as signing transactions and authorising AI agent requests.

The Atom sports a 6.77-inch OLED display, rear camera and 4,000mAh battery, and runs on a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip. It also incorporates a hardware privacy switch that physically cuts power to the camera and microphone.

The device also runs third-party apps, and will come preinstalled with Solana's Seeker app after Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner. Seeker combines Solana Mobile's wallet with its Solana dapp Store, which lists more than 1,500 decentralized apps, and will appear on Atom's home screen. Until now, the store was available on Solana Mobile's own Seeker phone.

Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that.

Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum… pic.twitter.com/vHhDNQYipz

Ledger Atom runs on the Android Open Source Project, the free, open version of Google's mobile operating system, alongside a Secure Element chip running Ledger OS. Its display and touch controls are physically isolated from Android, according to the release, and approvals in the Seeker app happen in a "Secure Mode" backed by the Secure Element.

"Having the Seeker app on Ledger Atom from day one just makes sense, so Ledger users get access to the Solana ecosystem without giving up any of the security," said Ian Rogers, Ledger's chief human agency officer.

Solana Mobile began opening its software stack to other Android manufacturers in March. Samsung Wallet also recently added USDC transfers on Solana. Seeker has handled more than $13 billion in transaction volume and 154 million transactions, according to the company, which says it has sold more than 200,000 devices across Seeker and its earlier Saga phone.

Hardware makers that integrate the stack can earn rewards in SKR, the native token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem, which also rewards users and developers, the release said.

Existing Seeker phones will remain fully supported, Solana Mobile said. Reservations for Ledger Atom are open now, though neither company has given a price or shipping date.

The Ledger Atom will include anti-tampering and tamper-evident features from the packaging to the device itself, according to the press release, including ways to help detect whether the enclosure has been opened, and will only be sold through Ledger's official site.

The announcement of the Atom comes at an awkward time for Ledger, as the firm investigates tampered devices in its reseller network linked to a suspected $87 million wallet drain .

The company this week disclosed that its Donjon security team had found an implant in a hardware wallet sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that captures recovery phrases during setup and sends them out over LTE. On Tuesday, it asked resellers in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to pull its devices from shelves.

Decrypt News Business Ledger Announces Atom Touchscreen Android Device

Ledger says the Android-based Atom will carry anti-tamper protections and be sold only on its site, as it probes tampered resold wallets.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Ledger has announced Atom, a touchscreen Android device that incorporates a Secure Element running Ledger OS.

Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner, with its Seeker app and Solana dApp Store preinstalled on Ledger's new Atom device.

The launch comes as Ledger investigates hidden implants found in hardware wallets sold through a reseller in Southeast Asia.

Ledger's new Atom device will ship with Solana's Seeker app preinstalled, the companies announced on stage at Ledger's Op3n conference in Paris on Thursday.

Billed as a "signer" rather than a hardware wallet, the Atom is an Android-powered touchscreen device equipped with a data-only eSIM and Ledger's Secure Element, enabling users to send and receive encrypted messages with other Atom users as well as perform crypto transactions in the manner of its range of wallets. To do so, the device switches into a Ledger OS-powered "Secure Mode" for sensitive operations such as signing transactions and authorising AI agent requests.

The Atom sports a 6.77-inch OLED display, rear camera and 4,000mAh battery, and runs on a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip. It also incorporates a hardware privacy switch that physically cuts power to the camera and microphone.

The device also runs third-party apps, and will come preinstalled with Solana's Seeker app after Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner. Seeker combines Solana Mobile's wallet with its Solana dapp Store, which lists more than 1,500 decentralized apps, and will appear on Atom's home screen. Until now, the store was available on Solana Mobile's own Seeker phone.

Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that.

Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum… pic.twitter.com/vHhDNQYipz

Ledger Atom runs on the Android Open Source Project, the free, open version of Google's mobile operating system, alongside a Secure Element chip running Ledger OS. Its display and touch controls are physically isolated from Android, according to the release, and approvals in the Seeker app happen in a "Secure Mode" backed by the Secure Element.

"Having the Seeker app on Ledger Atom from day one just makes sense, so Ledger users get access to the Solana ecosystem without giving up any of the security," said Ian Rogers, Ledger's chief human agency officer.

Solana Mobile began opening its software stack to other Android manufacturers in March. Samsung Wallet also recently added USDC transfers on Solana. Seeker has handled more than $13 billion in transaction volume and 154 million transactions, according to the company, which says it has sold more than 200,000 devices across Seeker and its earlier Saga phone.

Hardware makers that integrate the stack can earn rewards in SKR, the native token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem, which also rewards users and developers, the release said.

Existing Seeker phones will remain fully supported, Solana Mobile said. Reservations for Ledger Atom are open now, though neither company has given a price or shipping date.

The Ledger Atom will include anti-tampering and tamper-evident features from the packaging to the device itself, according to the press release, including ways to help detect whether the enclosure has been opened, and will only be sold through Ledger's official site.

The announcement of the Atom comes at an awkward time for Ledger, as the firm investigates tampered devices in its reseller network linked to a suspected $87 million wallet drain .

The company this week disclosed that its Donjon security team had found an implant in a hardware wallet sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that captures recovery phrases during setup and sends them out over LTE. On Tuesday, it asked resellers in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to pull its devices from shelves.

posts.content:
0.19% TRX $0.3325 0.14% LINK $12.51 0.91% ZEC $1,242.47 9.27% ADA $0.2305 0.93% XRP $1.33 0.81% ETH $2,455.66 1.57% BTC $82,241.37 0.58% XMR $545.34 0.87% BNB $730.58 0.31% XLM $0.1839 0.29% SOL $105.92 1.75% HYPE $82.10 1.55%

Written by Andrew Fenton staff editor Edited by Felix Ng staff editor Written by Andrew Fenton staff editor Edited by Felix Ng staff editor

Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion

Magazine Published Oct 15, 2026 The SEC and the CFTC have issued a raft of pro-crypto rules recently. But will the rules hold up in court, and can they be easily rolled back by the “anti-crypto army”?

In the wake of the failed CLARITY cloture vote in the Senate, the SEC and CFTC immediately moved to issue their own rules for crypto markets.

Two days after the vote, the SEC unveiled a five-year exemption that permits the issuing and trading of stock tokens. OXK has since teamed up with ICE to launch trading in 63 NYSE-listed stocks and Securitize launched 12 Securitize Stocks, including Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft.

The SEC has also issued guidance clarifying that a crypto token doesn’t become a security just because a project is buying back its own tokens, and stated that liquid staking tokens are not securities. It has also proposed new rules for the custody of crypto assets.

The CFTC, meanwhile, moved to exempt some crypto software providers from registration requirements. It has proposed a new “crypto asset market” registration category and intends to allow registered exchanges to offer leveraged trading.

But the concern among some in the industry is that these rules could be built on shifting sands . TD Cowen has cautioned that agency rules “are the easiest to rescind” — which was demonstrated when Trump-appointed commissioners wiped away all traces of the Gary Gensler era.

A 2024 Supreme Court decision also means agency rules can more easily be overturned by the courts.

The durability of regulator rulemaking is currently being tested in court, with a community bank group suing the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for exceeding its authority by allowing crypto firms to obtain national trust bank charters.

To discuss the legal issues involved, Magazine spoke with Yuriy Brisov from D&A Partners. This is an edited version of the conversation.

Magazine: SEC Chair Paul Atkins said after the CLARITY vote failed that the agency was releasing rules because Congress didn’t. Are agencies like the SEC supposed to create rules, or are they just supposed to interpret rules that already exist?

Brisov: They are supposed to create rules. They have this power under the Exchange Act of 1934. The SEC was created as a result of the major meltdown in the US markets in the end of the 1920s. From the moment of creation, the SEC had the power to create rules and regulations on how the laws should apply. American legislation works by creating general rules, like a frame, and then it has a watchdog watching over these regulations.

There was a reason why it was created like this — so that when, say, blockchain tokens came along, the US legislation would be ready to accommodate new technology. That’s what the Commission has been doing for ages now, and it’s obviously within their powers.

Magazine: Can they interpret the rules in the opposite way to an SEC appointed by a previous administration?

Brisov: There should be a reason for that. They can, in theory, do that, but it should be all within the formation of the body of law. Under Gary Gensler, the Commission tried to apply these rules to tokens. It turns out that it failed because there is still vagueness, and many companies left the US market for good.

This is the opening for the new Commission to oversee these rules and say, “You tried, but we can see that it’s not working. So we’ll offer our own rules.” But the power to offer rules is limited. If they offer some regulations that would lay an unbearable economic burden on companies, or something bizarre, there are also laws that allow companies or any damaged party to challenge this regulation in court and say, “We don’t like what the SEC has been doing because it’s damaging the market.”

In 2011, there was a case when the SEC applied new rules on how shareholders vote through a proxy. And the business community said, “it’s bizarre, it’s burdensome, and we don’t like it.” There was a case, Business Roundtable vs SEC, and [business] won.

Magazine: What was the Chevron decision by the Supreme Court and how does its overturning in 2024 impact court cases about rulemaking by agencies like the SEC and CFTC?

Brisov: Chevron was a famous case of 1984. The court basically said that if the law is vague or there are uncertainties and ambiguities in the statute, then we should use the agency’s interpretation as the law. In June 2024, Loper Bright was a new precedent that overruled Chevron. It’s now saying that we don’t have to. Of course, [the SEC is] a strong authority: Who knows securities laws better than the SEC? But the court should use its own brains and apply the Howey case itself.

Magazine: So that makes it more likely that SEC rules could be overturned?

Brisov: In some cases, the courts can come up with a different conclusion.

You cannot just come and say “we don’t like this regulation.” For instance, if you’re a traditional broker-dealer or traditional participant of the investment market in the United States and you say, ‘Look, I’m suffering because of this new regulation’ they should be able to prove that there was not enough research and that it’s burdensome for the business, and it’s not profitable for the US market. If they prove damages and if they prove a lack of research, then the court can overrule this regulation.

From what I can see, Paul Atkins and the SEC have been consulting with many crypto firms, with VCs. They’ve been doing their research, so it’s not something they just came up with within a day.

Related: OKX, NYSE parent file to launch tokenized US stock platform

Magazine: Let’s assume the SEC and CFTC rules survive for the next two years, and businesses invest a lot of money into infrastructure around tokenized stocks based on the new rules. Could a new SEC unilaterally reverse the rules or do they have to take into account the businesses built on top of the old interpretation?

Brisov: They have to take them into account. If there is the potential for the US market to grow and to benefit from this regulation, they won’t be able to just overrule it. There is the same thought process that either an agency or a court goes through. It’s called IRAC: issue, rule, analysis, conclusion. They would have to apply understandable, transparent logic.

They can’t just say we don’t like it. They have to explain. They have to bring up an economic background for it. They have to bring up research, and they have to prove that it’s insufficient. And only then can they come to a different conclusion.

For the sake of argument, we could say that Paul Atkins hates the Howey test, and he would have been happy just to abandon it — but he can’t do it. In every note, he keeps repeating that the Howey case still works, it’s still a valid regulation in the United States. However, we can interpret it in this case, and this case, differently — and this is our logic. This is what allows us to do that, and he explains it transparently.

Magazine: The SEC appears to have been working on the innovation exemption for years. But the SEC more recently came up with an FAQ saying that a crypto company buying back its own token does not make a commodity token a security. Could I be secure and comfortable launching a token buyback scheme on the basis of an FAQ by the SEC?

Brisov: If you follow it, and it’s created by the people who know what they’re saying, probably you will be in the clear. But it’s not legislation. An FAQ is just like a manual. It doesn’t have any authority, even for the staff.

Magazine: So the FAQ isn’t saying they changed the rules; it is just saying this is what the rules are?

Brisov: It’s just some extra explanation, like a casebook in the university. They are staff notes. A manual that explains for the staff how they should work and how they should understand this. They rewrite them quite often.

Magazine: They rewrote the FAQ after a week because a16z’s legal counsel said it left a massive loophole.

Brisov: Exactly, and that’s how it should be done. It’s not regulation or legislation, they can change them every week.

News Ethereum News Image by CryptoSlate Staking

Ethereum’s faster-exit plan would leave new validators waiting to earn

Faster exits would leave Ethereum’s entry cap in place. Direct validators wait to earn, while Lido holders share the cost of idle capital.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 EIP-8061 would expand exit capacity while retaining Ethereum’s 256 ETH activation cap per epoch, with no confirmed mainnet date. 02 Validator Queue displayed 1,282,776 ETH awaiting entry and an estimated 22 days, 6 hours when checked on October 15. 03 Lido core-pool holders can share rewards before their incoming ETH activates, spreading the earnings cost of idle capital across holders. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Ethereum staking could get faster exits under EIP-8061, but new validators would still have to wait for capped entry before earning rewards.

Validator Queue displayed 1,282,776 ETH waiting to enter staking and an estimated wait of 22 days, 6 hours when checked on Oct. 15. Its Oct. 14 snapshot, recorded at 21:17 UTC, showed 1,260,628 ETH and an estimated 21 days, 21 hours.

For a direct depositor, the delay postpones native staking income. A liquid staking pool such as Lido can give a new holder exposure to rewards from validators already working. The incoming ETH can still be waiting to activate, leaving more capital sharing those existing earnings.

Why Ethereum staking deposits wait to earn

EIP-8061 would retain the activation ceiling of 256 ETH per epoch. At 6.4 minutes per epoch, that amounts to 57,600 ETH a day when capacity is fully used.

The proposal would remove the fixed cap from exits and make exit capacity scale with active stake. It would also give validator consolidations their own capacity. Exits would remain rate-limited, even with a higher, stake-dependent allowance.

At 36 million ETH of stake, the authors’ worked example produces roughly four times the current capped exit capacity and twice the consolidation capacity.

As of Oct. 15, the EIP remained in Last Call, with a Nov. 1 deadline. Ethereum’s Glamsterdam roadmap listed it as scheduled for inclusion and expected mainnet in the fourth quarter, without a confirmed date. The mainnet consensus configuration had no activation epoch set for Gloas, Glamsterdam’s consensus fork.

A new direct validator deposit earns no native validator rewards while awaiting activation. Active validators earn ETH for their duties , so the economic hurdle is the time before that work begins.

The examples below use constant reward rates and exclude compounding, costs, taxes, penalties and alternative earnings. For 32 ETH inactive over the Oct. 14 snapshot’s estimated 21 days, 21 hours, or 21.875 days, multiply the assumed annual reward rate by 32 and by 21.875 divided by 365. This illustrates what an equally productive active stake could earn during that interval.

Assumed gross annual reward rate Illustrative gross rewards over the wait, 32 ETH 2% 0.038 ETH 3% 0.058 ETH 4% 0.077 ETH Applying a 10% rewards fee to those illustrative active-stake benchmarks gives about 0.035, 0.052 and 0.069 ETH. Lido’s token integration guide documents that fee rate. A solo validator need not pay it.

Related Reading A $1,000 MetaMask incident could turn Ethereum’s staking queue into a $5 billion traffic jam

When a user submits ETH to Lido’s mainnet core pool , the protocol issues stETH, its liquid staking token, and records the holder’s stake through shares. The funds can remain in the buffer or in Ethereum’s pending-deposit queue before earning native rewards.

Under Lido’s share accounting , a holder’s token balance reflects a share of the pool’s accounted ETH. That accounting includes buffered funds, active validator balances, pending deposits and deposits made since the last report. Lido’s separate staking vaults have their own collateral and share accounting; the example below concerns the core pool.

New core-pool shares can participate in subsequent reward distributions before the incoming ETH becomes productive.

If incoming capital stays inactive while existing validators produce the same rewards, those earnings are spread across more capital. Using the same illustrative 3% gross reward rate and 10% rewards fee makes the effect visible. If all capital is productive, the approximate holder rate is 2.70%. If 5% is non-earning, it becomes 2.565%; if 10% is non-earning, it becomes 2.43%.

Lido normally applies oracle-driven balance adjustments daily, but reports can be delayed and penalties can reduce balances. The fee is also governance-controlled.

Getting back to ETH follows different clocks

For an ordinary, unslashed full validator exit, the network schedules an exit epoch through the exit queue. An online validator performing its duties can keep earning while waiting; reward eligibility ends at the exit epoch.

The consensus exit rules then impose a separate withdrawability delay of 256 epochs, about 27.3 hours at 6.4 minutes per epoch. The balance reaches the withdrawal address through a subsequent sweep. Faster exit processing would address the exit-queue stage of this journey without eliminating the later steps.

Lido has another process. A holder locks stETH in a FIFO withdrawal request , waits for oracle finalization and then claims the allocated ETH. Finalization depends on available funds, timing checks and any relevant losses. CryptoSlate’s September coverage of that reserve explained how deposits and withdrawals can compete when the buffer is tight.

A secondary-market sale follows market conditions instead of the protocol’s withdrawal queue. Buying an existing stETH token transfers an outstanding claim; it does not require fresh ETH to pass through validator activation. Selling that token depends on available liquidity and market price, with no guaranteed immediate exchange for one ETH per stETH.

posts.title: Why Markets Are Dumping: Sticky Inflation Is the Problem Bitcoin Can’t Ignore
posts.titleVi: Why Markets Are Dumping: Sticky Inflation Is the Problem Bitcoin Can’t Ignore
posts.summary: September’s hotter-than-expected CPI report reignited fears that inflation is rising again, especially since the 3.7% annual increase was considerably larger than the 3.4% in August. Core CPI also rose to 2.6% year over year, above expectations and up from 2.4% the month prior.

posts.content:
September’s hotter-than-expected CPI report reignited fears that inflation is rising again, especially since the 3.7% annual increase was considerably larger than the 3.4% in August. Core CPI also rose to 2.6% year over year, above expectations and up from 2.4% the month prior. Gasoline jumped 9.1% in September alone, while shelter, airline fares, medical care, apparel, and other categories also moved higher.

This is what experts mean by sticky inflation: price pressures aren’t disappearing even after years of restrictive monetary policy. More importantly, they are spreading beyond one volatile category such as energy.

Analysts at the Kobeissi Letter noted that US inflation has stayed above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target for 67 consecutive months. It was last below that level during the COVID-19-induced lockdown in January 2021. The KL also outlined particularly sharp annual increases in several sectors: fuel oil up 74.2%, gasoline up 34.2%, airline fares up 22.4%, car repairs up 5.8%, hospital services up 5.6%, and electricity up 4.4%.

Persistent inflation creates a difficult environment for financial markets because it gives the central bank less room to lower rates and can even force it to raise them further, as it did at the September FOMC meeting.

Higher rates increase returns on relatively safe assets such as government debt while raising borrowing costs throughout the economy. Highly valued growth stocks in particular are hurt by this because future earnings are discounted at a higher rate and debt-funded expansion becomes more expensive.

The reaction was telling yesterday: the S&P 500 lost over 1%, the Nasdaq fell almost 2%, and technology and AI-linked companies saw a brutal sell-off. The Kobeissi Letter estimated that roughly $800 billion in S&P 500 market capitalization disappeared during the trading session, making it the worst day since late July.

BREAKING: The S&P 500 officially posts its worst day since July 29th, erasing -$800 billion of market cap.

Inflation is rising again in the US, now nearly double the Fed’s long-term target. https://t.co/aVXLApZrQA

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) October 14, 2026

Additionally, Asian markets fell sharply , with South Korea’s KOSPI down 8%.

Bitcoin wasn’t exempt from the broader market crash. The asset plunged to a monthly low of $80,200 earlier this morning after reacting negatively immediately after the CPI release. The concern is pretty straightforward: hotter and more persistent inflation means higher-for-longer interest rates and tighter liquidity, both of which tend to hurt risk-on assets.

Expectations for another rate hike during the upcoming October meeting skyrocketed after the CPI data went live. That shift matters for BTC because it doesn’t generate yield. When Treasury yields rise and cash becomes more attractive, investors have a stronger incentive to reduce exposure to volatile assets.

After it was rejected at $87,000 last week, bitcoin now fights to stay above $80,000 but the increasingly hostile macro environment spells further trouble ahead: sticky inflation, elevated rates, falling equities, ETF outflows, and leverage are all applying pressure at the same time.

Finance How Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI took down a massive crypto fraud network targeting Russian speakers

The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers.

By Francisco Rodrigues , AI Boost | Edited by Oliver Knight Oct 15, 2026, 8:35 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

Brooklyn took out the servers of crypto scammrs targetting Russian speakers Summary Show Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized or disrupted 241 scam websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto fraud that targeted Russian speakers in the US. The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers. Officials have seized about $300,000 so far. Crypto scams made up roughly 84% of the investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025.

Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI have seized or disrupted 241 websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto investment scam that allegedly stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims in the U.S.

The operation, carried out last week, came after a three-year investigation into a fraud network that relied on online infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said . No arrests were announced.

The scammers drew victims through Russian-language Facebook ads that promised investment opportunities. Fake advisers then called the victims and coached them to buy cryptocurrency and send it to fraudulent trading platforms.

When victims tried to withdraw their funds, the platforms locked their accounts or demanded more payments for supposed taxes and fees.

The scammers then “tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Gonzalez said. Recovered data showed they contacted victims a few weeks after the initial fraud, offering to retrieve the stolen funds.

The DA’s Virtual Currency Unit had previously seized or disrupted 400 domains tied to crypto investment fraud, but replacement sites kept appearing.

This time, investigators targeted the servers, hosted by Eastern European and U.S. companies, that held victim data and the software used to run the fraud. The goal was to stop the operators from quickly launching new sites.

The case comes as crypto investment scams accounted for roughly 84% of the $8.65 billion in investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025, according to the bureau’s annual report .

Across all internet-crime categories, crypto-linked losses totaled $11.37 billion, approximately 54% of the $20.88 billion overall. Both percentages are calculated from the FBI’s totals.

Brooklyn authorities have seized about $300,000 and are working to recover more. Prosecutors said some victims lost their entire life savings.

Finance How Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI took down a massive crypto fraud network targeting Russian speakers

The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers.

By Francisco Rodrigues , AI Boost | Edited by Oliver Knight Oct 15, 2026, 8:35 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

Brooklyn took out the servers of crypto scammrs targetting Russian speakers Summary Show Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized or disrupted 241 scam websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto fraud that targeted Russian speakers in the US. The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers. Officials have seized about $300,000 so far. Crypto scams made up roughly 84% of the investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025.

Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI have seized or disrupted 241 websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto investment scam that allegedly stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims in the U.S.

The operation, carried out last week, came after a three-year investigation into a fraud network that relied on online infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said . No arrests were announced.

The scammers drew victims through Russian-language Facebook ads that promised investment opportunities. Fake advisers then called the victims and coached them to buy cryptocurrency and send it to fraudulent trading platforms.

When victims tried to withdraw their funds, the platforms locked their accounts or demanded more payments for supposed taxes and fees.

The scammers then “tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Gonzalez said. Recovered data showed they contacted victims a few weeks after the initial fraud, offering to retrieve the stolen funds.

The DA’s Virtual Currency Unit had previously seized or disrupted 400 domains tied to crypto investment fraud, but replacement sites kept appearing.

This time, investigators targeted the servers, hosted by Eastern European and U.S. companies, that held victim data and the software used to run the fraud. The goal was to stop the operators from quickly launching new sites.

The case comes as crypto investment scams accounted for roughly 84% of the $8.65 billion in investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025, according to the bureau’s annual report .

Across all internet-crime categories, crypto-linked losses totaled $11.37 billion, approximately 54% of the $20.88 billion overall. Both percentages are calculated from the FBI’s totals.

Brooklyn authorities have seized about $300,000 and are working to recover more. Prosecutors said some victims lost their entire life savings.

Crypto scammers stole millions from victims, then returned pretending to help recover their money

Brooklyn prosecutors uncovered a second fraud targeting the same investors after dismantling infrastructure behind a multinational crypto scam.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Brooklyn prosecutors uncovered a crypto scam in which fraudsters stole millions, then approached the same victims offering to recover their money. 02 Authorities disrupted 112 servers and 241 domains supporting the scheme, which targeted Russian-speaking Americans and stole tens of millions. 03 Only $300,000 has been seized so far, leaving most stolen funds missing and victims facing uncertainty over possible restitution. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Crypto scammers who stole millions from Russian-speaking investors approached the same victims weeks later, promising to recover their losses.

On Oct. 14, Brooklyn prosecutors disclosed the fraud after an international enforcement operation disrupted 112 servers and 241 websites supporting a cryptocurrency investment scheme that allegedly stole tens of millions of dollars from victims across the United States.

The operation, conducted with help from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), targeted the infrastructure used to run fraudulent investment platforms and keep in contact with victims. Investigators recovered data showing the same criminal network tried to exploit people again after they lost money in the original scheme.

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said the scammers had targeted Russian-speaking Americans through an elaborate investment operation before attempting to extract further payments by offering to retrieve stolen cryptocurrency.

The investigation, which has been underway for three years, identified a concentration of victims in Brooklyn, home to a large Russian-speaking population. Some victims lost their entire life savings, according to prosecutors.

The recovered information also exposed how the fraudsters maintained relationships with victims beyond the initial theft, creating opportunities to solicit additional payments after their fraudulent investment platforms stopped processing withdrawals.

Prosecutors target servers behind repeat crypto scam

Investigators traced the operation to Russian-language Facebook ads promoting cryptocurrency investment opportunities.

People who responded to the ads received phone calls from individuals posing as Russian-speaking investment advisers. The purported advisers then directed them to cryptocurrency trading websites, helped them create accounts, and instructed them to purchase digital assets.

Victims subsequently transferred cryptocurrency to wallet addresses linked to the investment platforms, believing their money was being deployed in legitimate investments.

The deception typically became apparent weeks or months later when investors attempted to withdraw their funds. Some discovered their accounts were locked, while others were told they needed to pay additional fees or taxes before the criminals could release their money.

The criminals then exploited the losses they had created.

Prosecutors said recovered server data showed the operators contacted victims several weeks after the initial fraud, claiming they could recover the missing assets.

The second approach allowed the network to use information collected during the investment scam to target people already facing substantial financial losses.

Authorities did not disclose how many victims received these recovery offers or whether they made additional payments.

The findings mirror a broader pattern the FBI has identified, warning that fraudulent cryptocurrency recovery businesses often target people who have already lost funds to investment scams.

Such operations can demand upfront payments, provide misleading asset-tracing reports or falsely claim relationships with law enforcement agencies to persuade victims to send more money.

In the Brooklyn case, investigators concentrated on dismantling the infrastructure that enabled the criminal network to maintain its websites and repeatedly contact victims.

The District Attorney's Virtual Currency Unit had previously seized or disrupted about 400 domains linked to cryptocurrency investment fraud. However, replacement websites appeared quickly, allowing fraudulent operations to continue despite the enforcement actions.

That prompted investigators to expand their efforts beyond the websites themselves.

During an operation spanning three time zones last week, prosecutors executed search warrants and coordinated the disruption of cloud-based servers hosted by companies in Eastern Europe and the United States.

The criminal network relied on infrastructure and internet addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries to operate, according to the District Attorney's Office.

By targeting the servers, investigators sought to cut off access to the software, website data, and victim records the fraudulent platforms needed to operate.

The move also aimed to prevent the scammers from quickly rebuilding their websites and using stored customer information to approach existing victims with further recovery offers.

The enforcement effort involved cooperation from the FBI and several private-sector organizations, including Shadowserver, Coeus and UltaHost.

Despite the scale of the disruption, recovering the stolen cryptocurrency remains a separate challenge.

Related Reading Man sentenced to 12 years for $16M Coinbase customer support scam

Prosecutors estimate the scheme stole tens of millions of dollars, but investigators have seized only about $300,000 in stolen assets so far.

The District Attorney's Office has not disclosed whether victims have recovered any of those funds or provided a timetable for restitution. The announcement also did not identify the alleged operators or announce arrests.

Investigators continue efforts to recover additional assets, leaving most of the money stolen through the multinational operation unaccounted for.
